notes:
Sales/POC notes (shorthand):
- Company: Aperture UXWorks — mid-market SaaS, product analytics + in-app assistant. Replacing majority of OpenAI endpoints, evaluating Redwood Hosted first -> Dedicated.
- Primary contacts: CTO Maya Ortiz, Head of ML Lorenzo Kim. Buyer: VP Product (approval for Dedicated spend).
- Current infra: hybrid cloud (GCP primary), already using vendor X via API gateway for ~1.2M tokens/mo. Want to move to Redwood to reduce cost and get deterministic latency.
- POC scope: 3 endpoints mirrored for parity tests: (1) in-app chat (multi-turn), (2) semantic search (embeddings + ANN), (3) reranker for topN. Also one off long-form marketing copy generation test.
- Key metrics: target 95th pct latency <250ms for chat L1, embeddings bulk throughput 200 q/s, reranker tail latency <400ms. Cost sensitivity high: want 30-40% cost reduction vs current provider on steady state.
- Migration concerns raised: prompt parity (stop tokens, sampling seeds), streaming behavior differences, user-visible tokenization differences causing minor truncation, rate-limit model mapping.
- Found: embeddings parity OK. Reranker score drift ~12% for product taxonomy queries — likely due to tokenization + prompt framing; SE note: try prefix-cache + prompt-normalization.
- Long-form gen regression: Redwood model (hosted variant) produced shorter outputs and slightly lower factuality on sample set; raised red flag with product team. Quote from Lorenzo: "We can't ship regressions in product copy — need strict parity or a safe fallback."
- Compat-layer features requested: explicit stop_sequence handling, streaming chunk size controls, sampling seed control (deterministic runs for tests), and a 'parity-mode' that mimics vendor X's stop/stream behavior.
- Security: need SSO SAML, customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest, 1-year retention controls for logs, SOC2 + ISO27001 are table stakes. Asked for sample audit logs and KMS integration guide.
- Ops/Capacity: interested in Dedicated for stable throughput. Wants canary rollout and automated fallback to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity saturated. Also want predictable burst capacity for product launches.
- Pricing: they prefer a committed pool model (monthly) with defined burst headroom. Pricing sensitivity during procurement: internal budget range aligned to forecast.
- Next tactical items: finish parity checklist (Priya) by 3/12, hold Dedicated sizing workshop 3/17 with infra and finance, legal to send SOW by 3/20.
- Blockers: prompt parity regressions (high), compat-layer missing a couple of flags (medium), security attestation timeline (medium).
- Internal AE notes: escalate parity failures to runtime team — potential kernel/tokenization difference. Consider short-term workaround: route failing workloads to vendor X until parity fixed.
- Attachments/links: pricing deck in Drive, SOW draft (in progress), Fireflies transcript for 2/23 kickoff.
- Quote from CTO Maya on closing criteria: "If the POC shows parity (function + quality) and committed pricing matches our forecast, we'll move to Dedicated Q2."
